Memo:

Salesforce Q1 FY2026 (3M ended 2025-04-30) revenue grew 7.62% YoY to $9,829M. GAAP operating margin expanded 105 bps to 19.76% (from 18.71%), while non-GAAP margin expanded only 21 bps to 32.27% (from 32.06%). GAAP margin improvement was 5x larger than non-GAAP improvement, indicating the operating leverage claim in the analyst assertion is misleading: non-GAAP addbacks of $1,230M (63.3% of GAAP operating income) compressed the non-GAAP margin expansion.

Addbacks reconcile as 395 (purchased-intangible amortization) + 799 (SBC, excluding 15 already inside restructuring) + 36 (restructuring) = 1,230, with no double-counting of the 15 SBC overlap.

Q1 FCF was $6,297M (CFO 6,476 less capex 179), up 3.50% from Q1 FY2025 FCF of $6,084M. CFO-to-net-income was 4.20x in Q1 FY2026 vs 4.08x in Q1 FY2025. The six disclosed operating-asset/liability changes netted +$2,670M cash benefit (receivables +7,591 offset by capitalized contract costs -365, prepaid/other -481, AP/accrued/other -1,007, operating lease liabilities -124, unearned revenue -2,944), representing 54.1% of the $4,935M CFO-minus-net-income gap. This large working-capital contribution is typical of Q1 seasonality (customer collections, timing of vendor payments) and does not recur at the same magnitude in other quarters.

Q1 current ratio was 1.069x; quick ratio (cash + marketable securities + receivables) / current liabilities was 0.899x, down 0.029x from FY2025 year-end 0.928x. Net cash (cash + marketable securities - debt) was $8,973M at Q1 end, up $3,374M from FY2025 year-end $5,599M. Cash-only-minus-debt was $2,493M.

GAAP operating-income-to-accounting-interest-expense coverage was 28.56x (1,942 / 68); accounting interest expense is the correct denominator because it reflects the accrual-basis cost of debt capital incurred in the period, not the timing of cash payments (which was $28M in Q1 and subject to payment-date drift).

FY2025 FCF was $12,434M, up 30.91% from FY2024 FCF of $9,498M. FY2025 CFO-to-net-income was 2.11x vs FY2024 2.47x.

Mechanical annualization of Q1 FCF (6,297 x 4 = 25,188) is not appropriate: Q1 is unaudited interim data, subject to seasonality (working-capital timing, customer receipt patterns), and the filing warns interim results are not necessarily indicative of the full year. The analyst assertion that Q1 FCF is a "clean recurring earnings-quality measure" suitable for annualization is rejected: the $2,670M working-capital benefit (54% of the CFO-NI gap) is timing-driven, not recurring, and non-GAAP margin expansion (21 bps) was far smaller than GAAP expansion (105 bps), contradicting the claim of "equally strong operating leverage."

This analysis is not investment advice, makes no forecasts, and recommends no action.
